claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at room temperature.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at approximately 1000 °C.
Replacing Ta with Nb converts HfMoTaTiZr to HfMoNbTiZr.
Ta-to-Nb substitution will maintain a single-phase solid solution, such as BCC, in the as-cast alloy.
High configurational entropy and lattice distortion preserve phase stability in HfMoNbTiZr.
Nb is lighter than Ta, so replacing Ta with Nb decreases the alloy's average atomic mass.
The decrease in average atomic mass caused by Ta-to-Nb substitution lowers the alloy density.
Nb has atomic size and chemical characteristics sufficiently similar to Ta to support solid-solution strengthening.
Solid-solution strengthening associated with Nb substitution will preserve high-temperature mechanical performance comparable to HfMoTaTiZr.
HfMoNbTiZr will have a significantly lower density than 10.21 g/cm³.
HfMoNbTiZr will retain room-temperature yield strength and overall mechanical performance within approximately ±10% of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
HfMoNbTiZr will retain yield strength and overall mechanical performance near 1000 °C within approximately ±10% of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The expected density reduction from HfMoTaTiZr to HfMoNbTiZr is at least approximately 5%.
The proposed performance claim applies under quasi-static loading from room temperature to approximately 1000 °C.
The proposed performance claim does not address cyclic loading, high-strain-rate loading, or long-term environmental exposure.
Current evidence supports retaining mechanical strength within a ±10% threshold.

contradictions.description: The uncertainty field says that current evidence supports strength retention within ±10%, but no supporting evidence records are cited.
